contentHtml:
THE NETHERLANDS—Royal Philips will showcase Advanced Image Insights on HealthSuite, a cloud-based imaging solution, at RSNA 2026 in Chicago, USA, to help radiology teams integrate artificial intelligence (AI) analysis and advanced visualization into diagnostic workflows.

The solution combines Philips’ advanced visualization applications with centralized management of third-party AI tools.

Connected to Philips HealthSuite Imaging, it automates workflows and delivers analysis results directly into existing radiology systems, allowing radiologists to review findings alongside diagnostic images.

The platform also integrates with Philips Interactive Reporting Assistant, which combines clinical findings, key images and AI-generated results into structured multimedia reports.

The reports can include hyperlinks, tables and graphs, while voice recognition, automatic template selection and data population reduce repetitive documentation and manual data entry.

Integrating AI into radiology workflows

Philips is positioning Advanced Image Insights as part of its broader Healthcare Informatics portfolio, which connects imaging systems, software, data, AI and services through open platforms.

The company will demonstrate how these capabilities can help healthcare providers manage increasingly complex imaging workloads.

Radiology departments face rising imaging volumes, workforce shortages and growing pressure to deliver timely diagnoses.

Although advanced visualization and AI applications can improve image analysis, managing multiple disconnected tools often creates additional administrative work and complicates the transfer of findings between systems.

“The opportunity in radiology isn’t simply to add more AI applications, but to make intelligence work better across the diagnostic journey,” said Madhuri Sebastian, Business Leader Imaging Informatics at Philips.

She noted that integrating visualization tools and AI applications could reduce manual processes and give clinicians more time to assess images, review findings and make informed care decisions.

Advanced Image Insights supports applications across multiple imaging modalities, clinical specialties and healthcare sites.

Its integration with Philips HealthSuite Imaging picture archiving and communication system (PACS) enables automated access to analysis tools and allows radiologists to review their outputs within existing workflows.

For example, during a lung computed tomography (CT) examination, AI applications can analyse images for signs of incidental pulmonary embolism while other tools assess lung nodules.

The platform makes these findings available alongside the original images, supporting clinical review and reporting.

Radiologists retain responsibility for interpreting the images, evaluating AI-generated findings and making final diagnostic decisions.

Referring clinicians can also use the additional information to inform treatment planning and patient follow-up.

Cloud delivery and healthcare IT implications

Philips delivers Advanced Image Insights as a managed software-as-a-service (SaaS) solution through HealthSuite, powered by Amazon Web Services (AWS).

The cloud-based model provides remote access to advanced analysis tools, while Philips manages the underlying infrastructure and operations.

The approach could reduce the technical and administrative demands associated with deploying and maintaining imaging software across multiple healthcare facilities.

It also supports expansion across hospital networks and specialist departments without requiring each site to manage separate application infrastructures.

The launch reflects the growing focus among medical imaging technology providers on integrating third-party AI applications into established clinical systems.

As hospitals adopt more AI tools, interoperability, workflow integration, and centralised application management are becoming important considerations for healthcare IT investment.
